description.short_caption: Bronchoscopic view showing mucosal irregularities and exudates.
description.detailed_description: This bronchoscopic image shows the lumen of the tracheobronchial tree with visible mucosal irregularities and whitish exudates along the walls. The mucosa appears erythematous and inflamed, with some areas of thickened secretions or plaques. The findings suggest an infectious or inflammatory process affecting the airway.

description.short_caption: Bronchoscopic view showing mucosal abnormalities in the bronchi.
description.detailed_description: This bronchoscopic image shows the interior of the bronchi. The mucosa appears erythematous and irregular, with visible white plaques or lesions on the surface. The airway lumen is patent, and the bifurcation of the bronchi is visible. These findings may suggest an infectious or inflammatory process affecting the bronchial mucosa.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of endobronchial biopsy showing fungal mycetoma.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a round, dense fungal structure with concentric layers, consistent with a fungal mycetoma. The central core appears denser, surrounded by radiating filaments. The tissue is stained with a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) or similar fungal stain, highlighting fungal elements in pink and purple hues. The surrounding tissue shows minimal inflammatory response, suggesting colonization rather than invasive infection.
visible_findings: round fungal structure with concentric layers
central dense core with radiating filaments
pink and purple staining of fungal elements

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing septate hyphae with branching.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows fungal hyphal elements with septation and acute-angle branching. The hyphae are stained with a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain, highlighting their structure in pink against a lighter background. Cellular debris and inflammatory cells are visible in the surrounding tissue. The morphology is consistent with a fungal infection, likely from a septate hyphal organism.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing cytoplasmic inclusions in hepatocytes.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The field contains numerous cells with prominent cytoplasmic inclusions, some of which appear eosinophilic. The background tissue architecture suggests a hepatic origin, with scattered inflammatory cells and areas of cellular degeneration. The inclusions are consistent with viral cytopathic effects or intracellular accumulation of material.

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain showing fungal hyphae and conidia.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of fungal elements stained with lactophenol cotton blue. The fungal structures include septate hyphae and round conidia, with prominent spore-bearing structures (conidiophores). The stain highlights the fungal morphology in blue against a lighter background, aiding in identification. The image is likely from a culture preparation.
